_meta.gate: Phase 4 Gate 0 item (d). NOT production. The full 44-locale / 44-language analyzer port is Gate A.
how_this_is_applied: This document is BOTH a composable index template and the source of a create-index body.
NoDB does NOT rely on a server-side template to create repo indices: the alias name is
per-index (`<tenant>-<repo>`) and a composable template can only carry a STATIC alias, so
the alias must be attached in the create call. NoDB therefore issues an explicit
`PUT /<tenant>-<repo>+g<N>` whose body is this file's `template` object plus a computed
`aliases` block. `index_patterns`/`priority` below exist so the same file can also be PUT
to `_index_template/nodb-repo-v1` as a safety net for out-of-band index creation.
The generation that built an index records `_meta.templateVersion`; a template change is a
new generation (`+g(N+1)` rebuild), never an in-place mutation.

why_unambiguous: Tenant ids are control-plane-minted `^[a-z][a-z0-9]{2,30}$` and contain no '-', so the
FIRST dash is always the tenant/repo boundary even though repo ids may contain dashes.
'+' is illegal in a RepositoryId but legal mid-name in OpenSearch, so `+g<N>` can never
collide with an alias (aliases and indices share one namespace).
Names are constructed one-way from TenantContext; nothing security-relevant parses them
back — the authoritative alias→generation map is NoDB metadata.

generations.create: PUT <tenant>-<repo>+g1 with this body + aliases {"<tenant>-<repo>": {}}. One index kind per repo — Postgres replaced the ES storage index, so there is no `search`/`storage` discriminator.
rebuild: 1. PUT <tenant>-<repo>+g(N+1) with the NEW template, no alias.
2. Backfill from Postgres/outbox while the indexer double-writes both generations.
3. When g(N+1) has caught up to the g<N> checkpoint, ONE atomic call:
Alias actions are atomic in one cluster-state update, so readers never see zero or two
indices behind the alias. This is the mechanism for: analyzer/template changes, the V2
one-doc-per-version layout swap, shard-count changes (fixed at create), embedding-model
generations.queries: Always target the ALIAS, never a physical name. Multi-repo queries target the list of aliases in one request (DESIGN §5 / decision 1); `_index` in each hit is the PHYSICAL name, so repo/branch attribution must map physical → alias through NoDB metadata, not by string-parsing the index name.

dev_vs_cloud.shards: 1 in both. Index-per-repo means most indices are small; a large repo gets more shards at its next generation. Dev has one node, so >1 shard buys nothing.
dev_vs_cloud.replicas: DEV 0, CLOUD 1. XP's search-settings.json hardcodes number_of_replicas:1, which on a single-node dev cluster parks every index at YELLOW forever and makes `wait_for_status=green` health checks unusable. Overridden per environment, not per template.
dev_vs_cloud.override_mechanism: NoDB substitutes `number_of_replicas` and `refresh_interval` from cell config at create time; everything else is identical across environments so that collation keys and analysis are environment-independent.

refresh_interval_rationale: Kept at OpenSearch's default 1s, which is also ES 2.4's default — closest to today's
observable visibility behavior, so the Gate F byte-identical comparison is not perturbed
by a refresh-policy change on top of an engine change.
The §3.3 read-your-writes contract does NOT depend on this value: the indexer implements
`awaitRefresh(seq)` by waiting for the checkpoint to pass `seq` and then issuing an
explicit `POST /<alias>/_refresh` (or by writing the batch with `?refresh=wait_for`).
The background interval is only an upper bound on incidental staleness for readers that
* Tests should run with `refresh_interval: -1` so that ANY code path missing an explicit
awaitRefresh fails deterministically instead of passing on a 1s timer. Do not ship -1.
* `index.search.idle.after` (default 30s) is new since ES 2.4: an index with no search
traffic for 30s STOPS refreshing in the background, and the next search then blocks
until a refresh completes. Harmless for correctness, but it makes first-query latency
after an idle period lumpy and can mask/unmask timing bugs in the refresh tests.
* Cloud may raise this to 5s-30s for indexing throughput once Gate F parity is banked.

limits_raised_and_why.index.mapping.total_fields.limit: 1000 -> 10000. Did not exist in ES 2.4. XP emits one sub-field per (property x index-config suffix) — `_analyzed`, `_ngram`, `_path`, `_orderby`, `_orderby_<locale>`, `_stemmed_<lang>`, `_number`, `_datetime`, `_geopoint` — and because OpenSearch expands dotted names into OBJECT mappers (see es_24_isms), every path segment now counts against the limit too. A content repo blows 1000 easily. 10000 is a starting point; Gate A must measure the real count on the itest corpus and on a production-shaped content set.
limits_raised_and_why.index.mapping.depth.limit: 20 -> 50. Each dot in `data.a.b.c._analyzed` is now a mapping LEVEL, not part of a flat name. Deep content types plus the suffix segment can exceed 20.
limits_raised_and_why.index.mapping.nested_fields.limit: left at default 50 — the V1 layout uses no nested fields. Revisit for chunked-vector nested docs (DESIGN §5 roadmap).
limits_raised_and_why.index.max_result_window: left at default 10000 — same default XP already lives with on ES 2.4.6. Deep paging moves to search_after/PIT in Gate C.
limits_raised_and_why.index.max_docvalue_fields_search: left at 100. Flagged only because sorting on many `_orderby_*` fields at once would hit it.

_meta.es_24_isms_found: See es_24_isms below — every entry was verified by PUTting it against a live OpenSearch 3.7.0 with analysis-icu installed.

es_24_isms._note: Verified empirically against OpenSearch 3.7.0 + analysis-icu on 2026-08-05. Gate A owns the port; this is the list, not the fix.

hard_rejections.error: Failed to parse value [analyzed] as only [true] or [false] are allowed
hard_rejections.translation: drop; the field TYPE now carries the distinction

hard_rejections.error: Root mapping definition has unsupported parameters: [_all]
hard_rejections.translation: drop. _all is gone. XP also defines an `all_field_analyzer` (standard+lowercase+asciifolding+front_ngram) which has no consumer once _all is gone — Gate A must confirm nothing queries `_all` and delete the analyzer.

hard_rejections.error: Root mapping definition has unsupported parameters: [_default_]
hard_rejections.translation: drop the wrapper; mapping types are gone (single implicit _doc)

hard_rejections.error: The [edgeNGram] tokenizer name was deprecated pre 1.0. Please change the tokenizer name to [edge_ngram] for indices created in versions 3.0 or higher
hard_rejections.translation: edge_ngram. Also drop the `"side": "front"` param — it is silently ACCEPTED but has no effect in Lucene 10; front is the only behavior. Silent acceptance is worse than rejection: nothing will tell you.

hard_rejections.ism: "standard" used as a token FILTER in 5 analyzers (ngram_index_front, ngram_search_default, fulltext_search_default, document_index_default, all_field_analyzer, path_analyzer)
hard_rejections.error: The [standard] token filter has been removed.
hard_rejections.translation: delete the filter entry. It was already a no-op in late ES 2.x. THIS IS AN ANALYZER-BEHAVIOR CHANGE TO VERIFY, not a pure syntax fix — Gate D's corpus is what proves the token streams still match.

hard_rejections.ism: "ignore_above": 3072 on an ANALYZED (text) field — used by all 45 _orderby* templates
hard_rejections.error: unknown parameter [ignore_above] on mapper [f] of type [text]
hard_rejections.translation: ignore_above is valid on keyword and on icu_collation_keyword, not on text. This is an additional argument for the icu_collation_keyword rewrite below.

hard_rejections.error: accepted, but pins a single-node dev/CI cluster at YELLOW forever

BLOCKER_bare_string_field_vs_object.severity: HARD BLOCKER for Gate A. Nothing can be indexed until it is resolved. Found and reproduced at Gate 0.
what_xp_does: StaticIndexValueType.STRING has postfix "" — i.e. NO suffix — and
IndexItemFactory.create() ALWAYS emits the STRING variant for every indexed value.
So for one property `data.displayname` XP emits, in the SAME document:
The same applies to NodeIndexPath system fields: `_path` (bare) plus `_path._path`,
why_it_breaks: ES 2.4 with -Dmapper.allow_dots_in_name=true treated all of these as INDEPENDENT FLAT
field names. OpenSearch expands dots into objects, so `data.displayname` must be a leaf
(from the bare STRING variant) AND an object (parent of `_analyzed` etc.) at once.
-> can't merge a non object mapping [data.x] with an object mapping
-> mapper [data.y] cannot be changed from type [keyword] to [ObjectMapper]
-> can't merge a non object mapping [_path] with an object mapping
Note the order-dependence of the message: this is a real conflict, not a template issue,
and it fires on the FIRST document of every repo.
also_reserved_metadata: NodeIndexPath.ID = "_id" and NodeIndexPath.SOURCE = "_source" collide with OpenSearch
METADATA fields and are rejected outright as document fields:
{"_id":"abc-123"}      -> failed to parse field [_id] of type [_id]
{"_source":"whatever"} -> failed to parse field [_source] of type [_source]
ES 2.4 tolerated both. Gate A must rename or drop them (`_id` is already the document id;
XP's `_source` index field is unrelated to OpenSearch's stored _source).
options: OPTION 1 — RECOMMENDED, VERIFIED: give StaticIndexValueType.STRING a real postfix (e.g.
`_string`). Every emitted field then ends in a suffix and the object hierarchy is
consistent — siblings, never leaf-vs-object. Verified accepted:
{"data.w._string":"Hello","data.w._analyzed":"Hello","data.w._orderby":"hello"}
{"_path._string":"/a/b","_path._path":"/a/b"}
The whole end-to-end validation of this template used this shape and all query families
(term, fulltext, ngram-prefix, path_hierarchy, numeric range, date range, terms agg,
collated sort) work. Cost: the translator's field-name resolution must append `_string`
for the untyped/exact case, and this is a WIRE-VISIBLE doc-format change (Gate B).
OPTION 2 — change IndexItem.INDEX_VALUE_TYPE_SEPARATOR from `.` to a character OpenSearch
does not expand (e.g. `~`). Sub-fields become siblings of the bare leaf under the same
object parent, so no conflict either. Smaller doc-shape change than Option 1 but it
rewrites every field name the translator and every query construct 44+91 templates
refer to. Does NOT fix the `_id`/`_source` metadata collisions.
OPTION 3 — multi-fields: map the bare field as keyword with `fields: {_analyzed: ...}`.
REJECTED: multi-field values are DERIVED from the parent value, so XP could not ship an
independently computed `_orderby` (OrderByValueResolver may differ from the raw string),
which contradicts Phase 4 decision 3 (XP-shipped index documents). It would also force
every string property to carry every sub-field, defeating index-config opt-in.
GATE A MUST PICK ONE BEFORE WRITING THE INDEXER. It changes the index-document RPC shape,
so it also changes Gate B's wire serialization — decide before either is coded.
Good news: OpenSearch's stored _source preserves XP's ORIGINAL FLAT dotted keys verbatim
(verified), so whichever option is chosen, `_source` round-trips the shipped document and
the Gate G rebuild-from-docs drill stays viable.

silent_semantic_changes.ism: DOTTED FIELD NAMES — the mechanism behind the blocker above
detail: XP runs with `-Dmapper.allow_dots_in_name=true` (modules/runtime/src/bin/server.sh) and
builds FLAT field names like `data.title._analyzed`. In ES 2.4 that was one literal
field name. `index.mapper.allow_dots_in_name` no longer exists in OpenSearch 3.7
(verified: "unknown setting ... check the breaking changes documentation for removed
settings"), and dots in a document key are ALWAYS expanded into an object hierarchy.
CONSEQUENCE 1 (silent, severe): `"match": "*._analyzed"` matches against the LEAF
field name, which after expansion is just `_analyzed` — so `*._analyzed` never matches.
All ~91 dynamic templates stop applying and every field falls back to dynamic
text+keyword mapping. Verified: index create succeeds, indexing succeeds, and a term
query on `data.title._orderby` returns 0 hits with NO error anywhere.
CONSEQUENCE 2: object mappers now count toward total_fields.limit and each dot toward
depth.limit.
FIX (verified working): use `path_match` instead of `match` — `path_match: "*._analyzed"`
matches the full dotted path. Term queries and sorts on the dotted path then work.
`match: "_analyzed"` (bare leaf name, no wildcard) also works but is less explicit.
This template uses path_match throughout.
XP's 45 _orderby* templates are `type:string, index:analyzed, analyzer:icu_sort_<loc>`
and XP sorts on them directly. ES 2.4 allowed that via fielddata-on-by-default.
OpenSearch refuses: "Text fields are not optimised for operations that require
per-document field data like aggregations and sorting, so these operations are disabled
by default."
Option A (minimal, works): keep the analyzer form and add "fielddata": true. Verified
correct — sorts æ ø å — but loads collation keys into the heap-resident field-data
cache. On a shared multi-tenant cell that is a memory-pressure and noisy-neighbour
liability across 44 possible sort locales.
Option B (RECOMMENDED, what this draft does): `type: icu_collation_keyword` with the
locale in `language`/`country`, `index:false`, `doc_values:true`. Verified correct —
sorts æ ø å — with the collation key stored as a binary doc value, no fielddata, and
`ignore_above` legal again. The 44 `icu_collation_*` filters and 44 `icu_sort_*`
analyzers then only need to survive for any QUERY-time use of icu_sort_* (Gate A must
grep: if nothing but sorting uses them, 88 settings entries disappear).
GATE A MUST DECIDE A OR B. B is a mapping change, so it also changes what
`_orderby_<loc>` looks like on the wire — but not what XP SHIPS (still a plain string).

silent_semantic_changes.ism: ICU / CLDR VERSION IS PART OF THE SORT CONTRACT
detail: OpenSearch 3.7.0's analysis-icu bundles icu4j 77.1 (verified in the image:
/usr/share/opensearch/plugins/analysis-icu/icu4j-77.1.jar). XP's ES 2.4.6 analysis-icu
is ~a decade of CLDR older. Collation keys and therefore SORT ORDER differ between
CLDR releases for some locales. Two implications:
1. Gate D's icuSort tests may legitimately produce a different-but-correct order than
ES 2.4. That is the acceptance-rule conversation, and it is a DATA MIGRATION concern
for existing customers' saved sort expectations, not just a test concern.
2. Because icu_collation_keyword bakes the collation key into doc values at INDEX time,
an OpenSearch upgrade that bumps icu4j silently changes stored keys. Mixed-version
shards would sort inconsistently. This is precisely what the `+g<N>` generational
rebuild exists for: engine/ICU upgrade = new generation + alias flip, never in-place.

silent_semantic_changes.detail: search-mapping.json sets search_analyzer only for `*._ngram` (document_index_default). `default_search` (keyword tokenizer + lowercase + asciifolding) is the index-level default search analyzer for everything else — meaning a fulltext query string is analyzed as ONE keyword token unless the query names an analyzer explicitly. Gate A must decide whether that ES-2.4 arrangement is intentional XP behavior to preserve or an accident that the translator compensates for at query time. This draft sets an explicit `search_analyzer` per template instead of relying on `default_search`, which IS a behavior change — flagging it rather than hiding it.

silent_semantic_changes.ism: THE BARE/UNTYPED STRING FIELD HAS NO DYNAMIC TEMPLATE AT ALL
detail: search-mapping.json has templates for `*._analyzed`, `*._ngram`, `*._orderby*`,
`*._stemmed_*`, `*._path`, `*._number`, `*._datetime`, `*._geopoint` — but NOTHING for
the bare STRING variant that IndexItemFactory always emits. On ES 2.4 it therefore fell
through to the dynamic default: an ANALYZED string, index-time analyzer `standard`,
search-time analyzer `default_search` (keyword+lowercase+asciifolding, set as the
index-level default search analyzer). That is a mismatched pair — index-time splits on
whitespace, query-time does not — so exact-match behavior on the untyped field is an
ES-2.4 accident that XP's term/in/like/exists translation has been living with.
This draft maps it to `keyword` + `ignore_above: 8191` (template_string_default), which
is the intuitive 'exact value' behavior and what the structured-query families in Gate C
most likely want — but it IS a behavior change on the most heavily used field variant in
the system.
GATE A/C MUST RESOLVE THIS with the golden-query corpus, not by reasoning: run the
batch-1 term/in/like/exists corpus in ES mode, look at what actually matches on the bare
field, and decide keyword vs text-with-matched-analyzers. This is the highest-leverage
single mapping decision in the port.

silent_semantic_changes.detail: Good news: `{"type":"icu_collation","language":"no"}` still creates fine in OpenSearch 3.7 with NO deprecation warning header, despite being deprecated in Lucene since 5.0. So Option A above is available and the 44 filter definitions port verbatim. It is the SORT (fielddata) that breaks, not the filter.

All 40 are core Lucene and need no plugin: arabic armenian basque bengali brazilian bulgarian catalan cjk czech danish dutch english finnish french galician german greek hindi hungarian indonesian irish italian latvian lithuanian norwegian persian portuguese romanian russian sorani spanish swedish thai turkish + the custom light_nynorsk stemmer (verified accepted). ja/ko/zh are mapped onto core `cjk`, NOT kuromoji/nori/smartcn — so no analysis plugin beyond ICU is required. Gate A should note that `cjk` for Japanese is a bigram analyzer, materially weaker than kuromoji; the managed service offers kuromoji preinstalled and Sudachi as an optional package, so IMPROVING this later costs no infrastructure change.
